name: Tomato
description: Popular warm-season vegetable that produces nutritious fruits
careInstructions: Plant after last frost
Provide support with stakes or cages
Water consistently
Fertilize regularly during growing season

name: Lettuce
description: Cool-season leafy green that's easy to grow and harvest
careInstructions: Plant in cool weather
Keep soil moist
Harvest outer leaves first
Succession plant every 2 weeks

name: Carrot
description: Root vegetable that grows well in deep, loose soil
careInstructions: Direct sow seeds
Thin seedlings to prevent crowding
Keep soil consistently moist
Harvest in 70-80 days

name: Bell Pepper
description: Warm-season vegetable producing sweet, colorful peppers
careInstructions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost
Transplant after soil warms
Provide consistent moisture
Support with stakes if needed

name: Spinach
description: Nutritious cool-season leafy green
careInstructions: Plant in cool weather
Keep soil moist
Harvest young leaves
Bolt in hot weather

name: Zucchini
description: Prolific summer squash that produces abundantly through the season
careInstructions: Direct sow after last frost
Needs ample space to sprawl
Harvest when 6-8 inches long for best flavor
Check daily — squash grow fast

name: Cucumber
description: Fast-growing vine vegetable that thrives in warm weather
careInstructions: Plant after soil warms to 60°F
Train vines on a trellis to save space
Water deeply and consistently
Harvest when firm and dark green

name: Kale
description: Hardy superfood leafy green that withstands frost and cold temperatures
careInstructions: Plant in early spring or fall
Flavor improves after frost
Harvest outer leaves from bottom up
Very cold-hardy — grows in winter in mild climates

name: Basil
description: Aromatic herb perfect for cooking and companion planting
careInstructions: Plant after last frost
Pinch flowers to encourage leaf growth
Water at base to prevent leaf diseases
Harvest regularly

name: Oregano
description: Hardy perennial herb with strong flavor
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil
Drought tolerant once established
Trim back after flowering
Divide plants every 3-4 years

name: Parsley
description: Versatile biennial herb rich in vitamins
careInstructions: Soak seeds before planting
Keep soil consistently moist
Harvest outer stems first
Overwinters in mild climates

name: Chives
description: Perennial herb with mild onion flavor and pretty purple flowers
careInstructions: Very easy to grow
Cut like grass for harvest
Flowers are edible
Divide clumps every few years

name: Rosemary
description: Woody perennial herb with needle-like leaves and pine-like fragrance
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil
Very drought tolerant once established
Prune lightly after flowering
Protect from hard frost

name: Mint
description: Fast-growing aromatic herb that spreads readily and repels pests
careInstructions: Grow in containers to prevent spreading
Keep soil consistently moist
Harvest regularly to encourage growth
Can grow in partial shade

name: Thyme
description: Low-growing perennial herb with tiny fragrant leaves perfect for culinary use
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil
Excellent drought tolerance once established
Trim after flowering to keep compact
Overwinters well in most climates

name: Cilantro
description: Fast-growing herb used in cooking worldwide; leaves are cilantro, seeds are coriander
careInstructions: Direct sow in cool weather — bolts quickly in heat
Succession plant every 2-3 weeks for continuous harvest
Allow some to bolt and self-seed
Keep soil evenly moist

name: Marigold
description: Bright annual flowers that deter garden pests and attract beneficial insects
careInstructions: Direct sow after last frost
Deadhead for continuous blooms
Very heat tolerant
Self-seeds readily

name: Sunflower
description: Tall annual flowers that track the sun and produce edible seeds
careInstructions: Direct sow in spring after frost
Support tall varieties with stakes
Deep watering encourages strong roots
Harvest seeds when dried on stalk

name: Lavender
description: Fragrant perennial shrub prized for aromatherapy, culinary use, and pollinator attraction
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining alkaline soil
Excellent drought tolerance once established
Prune by one-third after first bloom to encourage bushiness
Harvest flower spikes just before fully open for drying

name: Rose
description: Classic flowering shrub beloved for its fragrant blooms and elegant form
careInstructions: Plant in fertile, well-draining soil with at least 6 hours of sun
Water at the base to prevent fungal disease on leaves
Deadhead spent blooms to encourage reblooming
Prune in early spring to shape and remove dead wood

name: Petunia
description: Prolific blooming annual with trumpet-shaped flowers in a wide range of colors
careInstructions: Plant after last frost in full sun
Water consistently — they wilt quickly when dry
Deadhead regularly or pinch stems to prevent legginess
Fertilize monthly for best bloom performance

name: Pothos
description: Easy-care trailing vine perfect for beginners; one of the most forgiving houseplants
careInstructions: Tolerates low to medium light
Water when top inch of soil is dry
Trim to maintain shape and propagate cuttings
Propagates easily in a glass of water

name: Snake Plant
description: Extremely low-maintenance upright plant that tolerates neglect and low light
careInstructions: Tolerates very low light conditions
Water sparingly — overwatering is the main risk
Allow soil to dry completely between waterings
Propagates from leaf cuttings or division

name: Spider Plant
description: Fast-growing plant that produces cascading baby plantlets on long runners
careInstructions: Bright, indirect light preferred
Keep soil evenly moist but not soggy
Allow plantlets to root in soil or water
Non-toxic to pets and children

name: Monstera
description: Iconic tropical plant with large split leaves, also known as Swiss cheese plant
careInstructions: Bright, indirect light brings out best leaf fenestration
Water when top 2 inches of soil are dry
Provide a moss pole or trellis for climbing support
Wipe leaves with a damp cloth to remove dust

name: Peace Lily
description: Elegant low-light plant that blooms with white spathes and purifies indoor air
careInstructions: Tolerates deep shade — great for bathrooms and offices
Water when leaves just begin to droop slightly
Mist leaves or use a humidifier for best growth
Toxic to pets — keep out of reach of cats and dogs

name: Strawberry
description: Sweet berries perfect for containers or garden beds
careInstructions: Plant in spring
Keep soil consistently moist
Remove runners for larger fruit
Harvest when fully red

name: Aloe Vera
description: Medicinal succulent with healing gel in leaves
careInstructions: Bright light
Well-draining soil
Water deeply but infrequently
Harvest outer leaves for gel

name: Jade Plant
description: Popular succulent with thick, glossy leaves
careInstructions: Bright light
Water when soil is dry
Can develop into small tree
Propagates from leaf or stem cuttings

name: Echeveria
description: Rosette-forming succulent with beautiful symmetry
careInstructions: Bright light
Well-draining soil
Water at soil level
Produces colorful flower spikes

name: Blueberry
description: Deciduous fruiting shrub producing antioxidant-rich berries in summer
careInstructions: Plant in acidic soil with pH 4.5-5.5
Mulch heavily with pine needles or wood chips
Prune older canes in late winter to encourage new growth
Net bushes when fruit begins to ripen to protect from birds

name: Raspberry
description: Vigorous cane fruit that produces sweet berries from summer through fall
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil with full sun
Provide a trellis or support system for canes
Prune spent floricanes after harvest
Mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds

name: Lemon
description: Evergreen citrus tree that produces tart fruit year-round in warm climates or indoors
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil or a large container
Needs at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight
Feed with citrus-specific fertilizer monthly during growing season
Protect from temperatures below 50 degrees Fahrenheit

name: Fig
description: Ancient fruit tree producing sweet figs in summer with minimal pest problems
careInstructions: Plant in a sheltered, south-facing spot
Water deeply but allow soil to dry between waterings
Prune in late winter to maintain shape and size
Wrap or mulch heavily in cold climates for winter protection

name: Sage
description: Aromatic perennial herb with soft gray-green leaves used in cooking and medicine
careInstructions: Plant in well-draining soil with full sun
Drought tolerant once established
Prune in spring to prevent woody, leggy growth
Replace plants every 3-4 years as they become woody

name: Dill
description: Feathery annual herb with a distinctive flavor, essential for pickling and seafood dishes
careInstructions: Direct sow in garden as dill dislikes transplanting
Succession plant every 3 weeks for continuous harvest
Allow some plants to flower and self-seed
Harvest leaves before flowering for best flavor

name: Zinnia
description: Vibrant annual flower that blooms prolifically in hot weather and attracts butterflies
careInstructions: Direct sow after last frost in warm soil
Space plants for good air circulation to prevent mildew
Deadhead spent blooms to encourage continuous flowering
Makes excellent long-lasting cut flowers

name: Cosmos
description: Tall, airy annual with daisy-like blooms that thrives in poor soil and attracts pollinators
careInstructions: Direct sow after last frost
Avoid rich soil and heavy fertilizing which reduces blooms
Pinch young plants to encourage branching
Self-seeds reliably for next year

name: Dahlia
description: Stunning late-summer to fall bloomer with intricate flower forms in endless colors
careInstructions: Plant tubers after last frost when soil warms
Stake tall varieties early before they topple
Pinch growing tip when plant is 12 inches tall for bushier growth
Dig up tubers after first frost in cold climates and store over winter

name: Pansy
description: Cool-season annual with cheerful face-like blooms that thrives in spring and fall
careInstructions: Plant in early spring or fall for best performance
Prefers cool temperatures and fades in summer heat
Deadhead regularly to extend blooming
Edible flowers that add color to salads

name: Chrysanthemum
description: Classic fall-blooming perennial with dense flower heads in warm autumn colors
careInstructions: Pinch stems back in early summer for bushier plants with more blooms
Plant in spring so roots establish before fall flowering
Water at the base to keep foliage dry
Mulch heavily in late fall for winter protection

name: Green Bean
description: Fast-growing warm-season vegetable available as bush or climbing pole varieties
careInstructions: Direct sow after last frost when soil is warm
Do not soak seeds before planting as they can crack
Provide trellis or poles for climbing varieties
Harvest frequently to encourage continued production

name: Garlic
description: Hardy bulb planted in fall for summer harvest, prized for culinary and pest-repelling properties
careInstructions: Plant individual cloves in fall, 4-6 weeks before ground freezes
Mulch heavily after planting to protect over winter
Cut scapes in spring to direct energy to bulb growth
Harvest when lower leaves brown but upper leaves remain green

name: Radish
description: One of the fastest vegetables from seed to harvest, ready in as little as 25 days
careInstructions: Direct sow in cool weather for best roots
Thin seedlings to 2 inches apart
Harvest promptly when roots reach mature size to avoid pithy texture
Succession plant every 10 days for continuous harvest

name: Broccoli
description: Cool-season crop producing nutritious green heads, with side shoots extending the harvest
careInstructions: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost or direct sow in late summer for fall crop
Transplant to full sun with rich, well-draining soil
Harvest main head while buds are tight and before flowers open
Continue harvesting side shoots for weeks after the main head

name: Sweet Potato
description: Warm-season root crop that produces nutritious tubers and attractive trailing vines
careInstructions: Plant slips after soil warms to at least 65 degrees Fahrenheit
Build raised mounds or ridges for best tuber formation
Water regularly during early growth, reduce as harvest approaches
Cure harvested tubers in a warm humid spot for 10 days before storage

name: ZZ Plant
description: Nearly indestructible houseplant with glossy dark green leaves that tolerates extreme neglect
careInstructions: Tolerates low light but grows faster in bright indirect light
Water only when soil is completely dry
Rhizome stores water so err on the side of underwatering
Wipe leaves occasionally to keep them shiny

name: Fiddle Leaf Fig
description: Statement houseplant with large violin-shaped leaves that commands attention in any room
careInstructions: Place in bright, indirect light and avoid moving once settled
Water when top 2 inches of soil are dry, using room-temperature water
Avoid cold drafts and sudden temperature changes
Rotate the pot quarterly for even growth

name: String of Pearls
description: Trailing succulent with bead-like leaves that cascades beautifully from hanging planters
careInstructions: Provide bright, indirect light to prevent sun scorch
Water only when soil is completely dry, about every 2 weeks
Use a well-draining cactus/succulent soil mix
Propagate easily by laying stem cuttings on moist soil

name: Hen and Chicks
description: Cold-hardy succulent that forms rosettes and spreads by producing offsets called chicks
careInstructions: Plant in gritty, well-draining soil or rock gardens
Extremely cold-hardy and drought tolerant
Separate offsets to propagate or let them form natural colonies
Mother rosette dies after flowering but offsets continue

name: Japanese Maple
description: Ornamental tree with delicate, deeply lobed leaves that turn brilliant red in autumn
careInstructions: Plant in sheltered spot with afternoon shade in hot climates
Mulch to keep roots cool and retain moisture
Prune minimally in late winter to maintain natural form
Protect from harsh winds which can damage delicate leaves

name: Hydrangea
description: Showy flowering shrub with large globular blooms that change color based on soil pH
careInstructions: Plant in morning sun with afternoon shade for best blooms
Amend soil pH to change flower color: acidic for blue, alkaline for pink
Water deeply and consistently as they wilt quickly in dry conditions
Prune after flowering on old wood varieties, or in spring for new wood types
